source_read: PMC HTML PMC8033773, full text (abstract, introduction, methods, results with Tables 1 and 2, discussion, limitations, future directions, conclusion, funding and competing interests); Figure 1 (PRISMA flow) not needed (counts are in the text); supplementary table (XLSX, results by outcome) not read

claims.overstatement: None; the claim is more cautious than the review. Aday et al. call these 'baseline measures' that 'predicted' the experience, although both Russ studies are flagged in Table 1 as retrospective, so the states were recalled after the experience; the claim's reframing ('recalled ... not predictors') is correct. Wording points: (1) all three r values come from one of the two studies (Russ et al., ref. 47, n = 143); for the other (ref. 46, n = 183) the review gives directions only, so 'in two retrospective online studies ... correlated strongly' should attach the sizes to the n = 143 study (the magnitude already says n = 143). (2) 'Online' is not stated for the Russ studies; it is implied only by the review's general remark on retrospective designs using online crowd-sourcing (Limitations). (3) The review itself calls surrender and absorption 'moderately to strongly' predictive; 'strongly' fits r = 0.72, less so 0.58.
claims.note: Numbers 0.72, 0.64, 0.58 and n = 143 found as stated. 'Rated critically low' is the editors' AMSTAR 2 judgment, not in the source; what the source shows is consistent with it (one database, PubMed; 4 of 14 studies added from outside sources; no risk-of-bias assessment tool for included studies; no protocol or registration mentioned; no meta-analysis). Separate caution: the review's own summary of Haijen et al. (2018) does not match Haijen's Table 7 (see anchor 4), so the review should not be cited for Haijen's findings; the claim cites Haijen directly, which is right.

anchors.locator: Results > Drugs > Psilocybin, 6th paragraph (Russ et al., ref. 47)
anchors.extracted: Retrospective psilocybin study, N = 143 (62 women): 'baseline' surrender r = 0.72 and absorption r = 0.61 with mystical-type experience; dread with preoccupation r = 0.64, confusion r = 0.58 and age r = -0.23; age and 'barriers' negatively related to mystical-type experience; the retrospective design could not control dose, setting or drug purity.

anchors.locator: Table 1 (Russ et al. rows, refs. 46 and 47; footnote a); Results > Drugs > Psilocybin, 5th paragraph (Russ et al., ref. 46)
anchors.extracted: Both Russ et al. (2019) studies are marked as retrospective designs: unselected people who used psilocybin, varied doses, no control condition, N = 183 and N = 143. For ref. 46 the review reports directions only: preoccupation and confusion positively related to adverse reactions, openness negatively; surrender, absorption and spiritual motivations positively related to mystical-type experience and ego dissolution; apprehension and deservingness negatively.

Authors: many included studies had open-label designs, small or homogeneous samples; retrospective designs using online crowd-sourcing may carry self-selection bias; many relationships not yet replicated; unpublished null results (file drawer) may exist.

anchors.locator: Results > Drugs > Psychedelics Not Otherwise Specified, 1st paragraph; Table 1 (Haijen et al. rows); Table 2 ('set' row)
anchors.extracted: The review states that a clear intention and a positive set were conducive to mystical-type experiences and visual effects and decreased the likelihood of a challenging experience. In Haijen et al. (2018, Table 7) set was not related to mystical-type (0.014, p = 0.835) or visual scores, and clear intentions was not significantly related to challenge (p = 0.088). Table 1 gives the set-challenging direction as '+', Table 2 as '-'.

anchors.locator: Methods > Search Strategy, 1st paragraph; Methods > Selection Criteria, 1st paragraph; Results > Study Selection, 1st and 2nd paragraphs
anchors.extracted: PubMed only; 6 drug terms x 7 predictor terms = 42 searches; English, human, 1994 onward; 1,635 records; 10 met criteria plus 4 identified from outside sources = 14 studies (10 psilocybin, 2 LSD from one sample, 1 ayahuasca, 1 mixed). Two authors searched independently; no risk-of-bias tool for included studies is described; narrative synthesis.

key_findings.correction: Locator detail only: the Limitations heading sits under the Discussion (Discussion > Limitations, 1st paragraph).

reporting_issues.note: Recomputed from Table 1: mean 237.5 (SD 517.0) with Haijen as 212, 269.1 (SD 528.7) with 654; the 1993 value alone forces SD above 522 if the mean were 108.75.
Checked against Haijen 2018 Table 6 in this session: openness x time 1.500 (p = 0.002) at baseline, 1.273 (p = 0.030) at 2 weeks.

risk_of_bias.note: AMSTAR 2 critically low follows from unmet critical items 2, 4, 7, 9 and 13, all consistent with the full text (PubMed only, 4 of 14 added ad hoc, no risk-of-bias tool, no protocol).

interpretation_gap.note: 'Substantial' fits; the quoted Conclusion phrase is exact. One nuance in the card's analysis field (not a key finding): 'absorption was equally associated with challenging experiences' overstates slightly; in Haijen 2018 the coefficient was 0.215 for challenge against 0.347 for mystical-type.

missed: The card's exposure field calls both Russ 2019 studies 'online samples'; the review never says so for those studies, and the only basis in the review is the general Limitations remark about retrospective designs using online crowd-sourcing (true or not of the primary studies, it is not stated in this source).

Table 2's openness row cites ref. 54 (Haijen 2018) alongside 46 and 48, although none of the outcomes listed there (adverse experience, oceanic boundlessness, mystical experience) come from Haijen; a further citation mismatch in the same family as reporting issues 1 to 4 and 8.
